title: Sandra Bullock Recalls Seeing UFOs and Says Government Files Made Her Feel 'Not Insane'
excerpt: Sandra Bullock recalls seeing five lights in Saint Martin and says government documents later left her feeling 'vindicated'.
content:
Sandra Bullock says she no longer felt 'like an insane person' about a mysterious sighting over St Martin after reading government files on unidentified aerial phenomena which, in her view, appeared to mirror what she saw and gave her the confidence to talk about it publicly for the first time.

The actor said the documents seemed to support an unexplained incident she kept private for years while filming on the Caribbean island.

Sandra Bullock's UFO Account

Speaking on the 'NGL with Kylie' podcast, Bullock said she had been on a beach with a group of people after filming when she noticed a light travelling across the sky. She initially believed it was a satellite.

A second light then approached from another direction, followed by several more, she said. Bullock said she considered whether the lights could have been aircraft, but they stayed in position until five had appeared.

'There was five all together, and they all came together,' Bullock said. 'All of a sudden they just took off.'

The 'Miss Congeniality' actor said she looked around to ask whether anyone else had seen the lights. She said she thought one of the others present had also witnessed the moment.

Bullock described the incident as a one-off and did not say she had experienced a similar sighting since. She did not identify the film production, the date of the incident or the people who were with her.

Government Files and Bullock's Response

Bullock said she did not discuss the sighting publicly until the release of government documents relating to unidentified aerial phenomena. She told podcast host Kylie Kelce that an 'exact formation' resembling the one she described had also been seen by 'legitimate pilots'.

'And then I was just quiet about it until the government released the documents,' Bullock said. 'So I feel... vindicated.'

She also said: 'I'm so happy that the government has finally corroborated my story, so I no longer feel like an insane person.'

The statement reflects Bullock's interpretation of the released material rather than confirmation that officials verified her individual sighting.

The distinction is central to Bullock's account: she says similar reports in government material persuaded her that she had not imagined the experience.

The source does not identify the documents she read, the pilots she referenced, or an official finding linking her account to a specific reported incident.

Why Bullock Thinks Aliens are Here

Bullock went beyond recounting the St Martin sighting when asked about whether alien life could exist. She said she believed aliens could already be present, describing them as 'watching and laughing' while remaining invisible.

'I think they're here,' Bullock said. 'I think they're here, watching and laughing. But they're invisible.'

Her remarks have drawn attention because they combine a detailed personal account with a claim that released government files made her feel validated. The interview has also been shared in a social media video clip, bringing the comments to a wider audience.

Bullock is widely known for films including 'Miss Congeniality' and 'Gravity', but said she had not spoken about her own experience until after reading the material she believed related to it. Her account remains a personal recollection of unexplained lights rather than evidence establishing their origin.
